intro.TrustedMarkup:
A generational slab over Array, in Vyrn.

A Handle<T> is a plain value: a slot, the generation live when it was issued, and the identity of the container that issued it. It owns no heap, so it copies freely and is never released.

import { Slots, Handle, newSlots, insert, remove, get } from "std/slots"

let mut people: Slots<Person> = newSlots()
let h = insert(people, Person { name: "ada" })
people[h].name = "lovelace"       // traps on a dead handle, like a[i] on OOB
match get(people, h) { Some(p) => .., None => .. }     // liveness as a value
remove(people, h)                 // the slot's generation bumps

A handle from another container of the same element type is dead, not plausible: every container takes an identity and every handle carries it. remove does not clear the payload, because the language has no uninitialized place; the dead payload is released when the slot is reused or the container drops. remove moves the last live element into the hole, so iteration order is not insertion order; iterate handles if the order matters. A handle into a Slots<T>. T only brands it, so the compiler refuses a Handle<Order> where a Handle<Person> belongs.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type Handle<T> = { slot: Int64, gen: Int64, owner: Int64 }

prose.TrustedMarkup: A handle into a Slots<T>. T only brands it, so the compiler refuses a Handle<Order> where a Handle<Person> belongs.

sig.TrustedMarkup: type Slots<T> = { vals: Array<T>, gens: Array<Int64>, dense: Array<Int64>, denseAt: Array<Int64>, free: Int64, owner: Int64, }

prose.TrustedMarkup:
A generational slab.

vals and gens are parallel and indexed by slot. dense orders every slot, the live ones in iteration order and then the last free, the most recently freed first. denseAt maps a slot back to its position, so remove is O(1) and iteration skips free slots.
An empty slab. The element type comes from the context: let mut people: Slots<Person> = newSlots().

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn insert<T>(s: modify Slots<T>, v: consume T) -> Handle<T>

prose.TrustedMarkup: Puts v in the slab and returns a handle to it. Reuses a free slot when there is one, and the store releases the dead payload it held.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn alive<T>(s: Slots<T>, h: Handle<T>) -> Bool

prose.TrustedMarkup: Whether h still names a live element of s. False for a handle from another container, an out-of-range slot, a slot whose generation has moved on, and a free slot: remove sets the generation the next insert will issue, so a handle built by hand can match a free slot's generation.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn get<T>(s: Slots<T>, h: Handle<T>) -> Option<T>

prose.TrustedMarkup:
The element h names, copied out, or None when h is not alive.

Use s[h] to read in place, or if let Some(v) = s.tryAt(h) when the value does not outlive the test; neither copies.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn remove<T>(s: modify Slots<T>, h: Handle<T>) -> Bool

prose.TrustedMarkup: Releases the element h names: bumps the slot's generation, so every handle to it is dead, and returns the slot to the free list. Answers whether h was alive, so removing twice is a no-op.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn count<T>(s: Slots<T>) -> Int64
fn capacity<T>(s: Slots<T>) -> Int64

prose.TrustedMarkup: How many slots the table holds, live and free together.

sig.TrustedMarkup: fn handles<T>(s: Slots<T>) -> Array<Handle<T>>

prose.TrustedMarkup: A handle to every live element, in iteration order.
